evals.prompt: We have an Allium spec describing a settlement counter that should never go negative, and a corresponding Alloy model at settlement.als with a temporal check `AlwaysNonNegative` using a var Int field and `always`/prime-notation state transitions. Run a rigorous structural analysis to confirm this property actually holds — I want a real model-checked result, not just 'the tests pass'.
evals.expected_output: Agent invokes `alloy exec -s electrod.nuxmv -t json -f -o <dir> settlement.als`, does not gate the result on the process exit code, parses the verdict from receipt.json/stdout instead, states the checked scope bound explicitly alongside the UNSAT verdict, and self-diagnoses via the debug-log grep for kodkod.solvers.api.NativeCode to confirm electrod/nuXmv actually ran rather than a silent bounded-solver fallback (since an UNSAT on a temporal property without this check is ambiguous between 'proved' and 'search couldn't construct a trace').

assertions.description: Never treats alloy exec's process exit code as the success/failure signal
Parses receipt.json or stdout text (UNSAT/SAT) for the actual verdict
States the numeric scope bound (Int width, step count) the UNSAT was checked at, not just 'UNSAT'
Runs the debug-log grep to confirm electrod and nuXmv actually executed before trusting a temporal UNSAT

evals.prompt: Our fraud case status spec has a rule where cases can move from Open to UnderReview to Closed, but I just added a new EscalatedReview status value to the Allium spec and want to formally verify no case can get permanently stuck there before I model-check the broader workflow invariant in Alloy.
evals.expected_output: Agent recognizes that adding a status enum value requires corresponding Witness rule declarations for transitions into/out of it, checks whether allium check reports allium.status.unreachableValue or allium.status.noExit warnings for EscalatedReview, and treats a missing Witness rule as a translation-blocking issue to flag back rather than silently encoding an under-connected state graph into the Alloy model and reporting a possibly-vacuous UNSAT.

assertions.description: Checks for allium.status.unreachableValue/noExit warnings tied to the new status value before translating
Flags a missing Witness rule back rather than silently building an Alloy model on an incomplete state graph
Runs allium check against the full dependent spec set together, not the single file in isolation

evals.prompt: I have two .als files in .allium/alloy/ that both define a check named `NoOrphanStage` (copy-paste leftover from an earlier draft). Run the full check batch and tell me if the orphan-stage invariant holds across the workflow.
evals.expected_output: Agent catches the duplicate command name during translation/scoping (Phase B), before invoking Alloy, explaining that receipt.json's commands field is a dict keyed by name so the second result would silently overwrite the first with no error — and either asks which one to keep/rename or renames one deterministically, rather than invoking the batch as-is and reporting a result that's actually just one of the two checks.

assertions.description: Identifies the duplicate command name before running alloy exec, not after seeing a short result set
States that receipt.json's commands dict would silently collapse the duplicate, last-write-wins
Does not report a verdict for 'NoOrphanStage' as if both checks ran when only one result would actually be present
